ai.description: This lizard reaches 12 cm in total length. It is pale sandy-brown with dark dorsal spots and a white underside. Key features include a shovel-shaped snout and a distinctively fringed, toad-like head.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Bufoniceps laungwalaensis* is uniquely identified by the presence of a distinct, prominent fold of skin across its throat, which is absent in other Indian toad-headed lizards.
ai.habitat: *Bufoniceps laungwalaensis* inhabits the hyper-arid, sparsely vegetated sand dunes of the Thar Desert, specifically favoring areas with *Calligonum polygonoides* shrubs.
ai.behavior: The Laungwala toad-headed lizard is primarily crepuscular, emerging during dawn and dusk to forage for insects while avoiding the extreme heat of the Thar Desert.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Bufoniceps laungwalaensis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 2–3 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Bufoniceps laungwalaensis* is endemic to the Thar Desert in Rajasthan, India, where it inhabits low-elevation, sandy dune environments.
